claims.text: Temporal Workflow history is bounded at 51,200 events or 50 MB, with warnings after 10,240 events or 10 MB, so long-lived agents need history management.
Temporal Continue-As-New passes state into a fresh execution with the same Workflow ID, a new Run ID and fresh history, and helps move long-lived work off old code versions.
Temporal Activity retries default to exponential backoff with a 1-second initial interval, coefficient 2, 100-second maximum interval and unlimited attempts.

Temporal Activities can complete an external write and crash before reporting completion, causing a retry; Temporal recommends idempotent Activities, and Run ID plus Activity ID is a documented key stable across retries.

In Temporal, deterministic agent coordination runs in a Workflow while nondeterministic LLM, tool and API calls run in Activities; recorded Activity results are reused on replay instead of regenerating model output.

Emergent reports over 1 billion Temporal Actions per month, with agentic app builds taking 10-30 minutes, Child Workflows orchestrating subagents, and builds recovering from node/pod failures and deployments.
Town reports 1.5 billion monthly Temporal Actions, up from roughly 150 million after launch; agents can wait 45 days for follow-up and unanswered email-send approvals expire after seven days.
Jota reports about 180 million Temporal Actions per month for its Jota 2.0 financial agent, which reached 100% of users and showed roughly 3x engagement versus the prior generation in A/B testing.

Sherlocks AI dispatches 10-15 specialized agents per incident on Temporal, with complex investigations taking 15-20 minutes; retries can lower reasoning settings or fall back to another model, and Signals let engineers add evidence or cancel subagents.
Replit says Restate now handles all its durable agent orchestration, replacing Temporal, and a promotional spike reached close to 25,000 durable actions per second per cell.

Restate's default inactivity timeout is one minute without new journal entries, after which it suspends and retries the invocation, so long LLM calls may require raising timeouts; Restate Context operations cannot be nested inside ctx.run.
Restate pins invocations and retries to the deployment version they started on and advises against handlers lasting days or months that would force retaining old deployments.
Aient runs its AI DevOps backend entirely on Restate with roughly 87 controller loops/services, and sessions lasting hours or days.
Inngest limits are 1,000 steps per function, 4 MiB per step result and 32 MiB total run state; maximum run duration is 30 days Free, 90 days Pro, 366 days Business.
Inngest steps get one initial attempt plus up to four retries by default, with per-step retry counts and non-retriable errors for permanent failures.
Inngest event deduplication has a 24-hour window and does not make external tool calls idempotent; a stable business-operation key or duplicate-safe write is needed.

Inngest reports its Insights AI query latency fell from 15-30 seconds to 3-6 seconds after enabling checkpointing, and that switching from GPT-4 to Claude raised success from about 50% to 90% in informal testing of 50 questions.
cubic reports a 51% reduction in false positives after moving its code-review system from one agent to a multi-agent design on Inngest, with idempotency addressing races between parallel agents.
Inngest step.waitForEvent() supports human approval with a timeout, and the function is suspended while waiting with no compute cost.
DBOS step retries are disabled by default; when enabled the defaults are three attempts, one-second initial delay and exponential backoff factor 2.
DBOS sleeping or receiving workflows remain in memory by default; suspension that frees memory and queue capacity is a DBOS Transact Enterprise feature.
DBOS steps are at-least-once, so interrupted external calls can run again, while DBOS transactions commit exactly once.

Goblins reports moving production workflows from Inngest to DBOS after an Inngest outage left a backlog it could not clear, with workflows taking 2-3 seconds directly versus over nine seconds on Inngest; this is customer/vendor-reported.
Dosu's AI ingestion pipeline on DBOS scaled to 20,000 workflows per hour, serving over 50,000 customers; the figure covers the ingestion pipeline, not agent sessions.
Cortex added an on-disk journal keyed by operation ID after a micro-VM vanished during git clone, combining DBOS at-least-once execution with application idempotency to get effectively-once effects.
